source: Read-only Android dumpsys location and same-signature metadata probe; pinned host 1.0.10 smali; no coordinates, audio or diary content in this evidence

historical_statistics.window: since system location statistics began; not one day

code_findings.existing_dev161_policy: Only failed background one-shot retries: 60 seconds then 300 seconds; cache/in-flight/foreground/continuous unchanged

limits: Current connected observations establish high-frequency background GPS activity, not its share of the reported 2900mAh or daily battery savings.
No new unconnected-glasses battery test was performed; earlier dev161 retry evidence remains separate.
No product location policy was changed. Next work must establish the lifelog/navigation ownership boundary before applying a lower-power lifelog policy.
findings: Normal dev164 cold start followed by Home retains a 5-second HIGH_ACCURACY GPS request and receives GPS locations through the observation window; this is not merely network/cache updates or an instrumentation-only effect.
Warm background run stopped GPS for the sampled 90 seconds, but a later registration was observed. Background GPS cannot be described as either always off or always on.

Connected background instrumentation recorded zero foreground samples, committed AMap continuous updates, and a roughly five-second fresh cache; one-shot generation stayed at 2 with no waiters or active one-shot client.

Runtime configuration uses 30-second logical/summary intervals but 5-second source intervals and no delivery throttling. The native AMap builder uses sourceIntervalMillis with Hight_Accuracy and GPS-first.
Existing dev161 backoff only limits failed one-shot retries; it does not regulate successful continuous location. New lifelog text upload code does not start location.

Original LifeLogLocation and GlassesNavigationLocation runtimes share the native location API; its settings argument has no caller-purpose field. Blanket background stop/interval change could degrade navigation and is not applied.

observation_limits: UI was not continuously sampled during the normal background run; Home was explicitly sent, and another app was foreground at follow-up. Instrumentation independently recorded zero foreground samples.
Android event wall times vary by about one millisecond between dumps; repeated snapshots are not summed as request counts.
Normal warm and cold results differ; an async startup race is not yet proven.

probe_field_correction: Legacy continuous_preparing reports M1.j (requested continuous state), not proof of a stuck startup. Diagnostic source now names it continuous_requested; raw report fields retained for traceability.
